title: Use These Three leadership Actions to Supercharge Employee Motivation
author: Kurt Mueller
summary: Mueller argues that leaders can raise motivation, and with it productivity, engagement, satisfaction and retention, by pulling three levers: autonomy, mastery and making a difference. He explains how autonomy builds ownership, tailored work and creativity, how developing capabilities through training, stretch assignments and recognition feeds confidence, and how communicating purpose, delegating decisions and giving feedback make people feel their work matters. He cautions that autonomy must be balanced with accountability. The piece is a generic but clearly organised framework for managers rather than original research.
points: Motivated employees deliver productivity, engagement, satisfaction, retention and talent attraction that reflect on the leader.
Autonomy builds ownership and creativity, provided it is balanced with accountability.
Mastery is motivated through training, challenging assignments and tying growth to recognition and advancement.
Making a difference depends on communicating purpose, delegating decisions and giving regular recognition and feedback.
quotes: However, it's important to strike a balance between autonomy and accountability, ensuring that employees have the freedom to make decisions while also being responsible for the outcomes of their choices.
When employees see that their organization is invested in their professional growth, it fosters a sense of value and importance.
Assigning challenging tasks, projects, or goals that require employees to stretch beyond their current capabilities can be a motivating factor.
Employees need to understand how their work fits into the larger mission and goals of the company.
Constructive feedback is also valuable as it helps employees understand how their actions contribute to success and how they can make an even greater impact in the future.
